Before anybody presents anything, I want to say something about the paper we tried to repeat last month, because I think it is the most useful thing that happened to this group all year. We chose it because the result was interesting and because it looked simple. Four weeks later we had spent about nine hundred reais of consumables and we still did not have their result, and here is the part that matters: we are now fairly sure the work is fine. The paper is not. Three things were missing. The temperature at which the samples were stored between collection and analysis, which turned out to be the whole thing. Whether the replicates were pooled before or after the first measurement, which the text simply does not say. And a single sentence about the control group that could be read two ways. Nobody was hiding anything. Somebody wrote the section, read it back, and it made perfect sense to them, because they had been standing there. So when you write yours, the test is not whether it is true. The test is whether somebody in another building could run it on a Tuesday without emailing you.

Hi, it is me, I am leaving this now because you asked me to keep an eye on your samples while you were away and I want you to have the order right rather than my summary of it. So. On Monday the tubes were taken out of the freezer and thawed on the bench, not in the water bath, because the water bath was broken again. They were left for about forty minutes. Prior to any of that, and this is the bit you did not ask for, the whole rack had already been relabeled, because two of your labels had come off in the freezer and I did not want to guess. On Tuesday the replicates were pooled, three into one, and then the first measurements were taken. Following that, everything went back at minus twenty. Your control group was not touched at any point, which I assume is what you wanted. One thing I am not sure about, and you should write it down before you forget: I do not know whether the tubes had been thawed once before, in June. Ask the person who ran it then, because I genuinely do not know, and it belongs in your methods.
